## Design

### 2026-10-06 – Monday Oct 5 - I finally got my starbie design done

**4h**

Monday Oct 5 - I finally got my starbie design done

I just followed the tutorial on how to make a starbie! I started akwardly by using the wrong part and wondering why mine didn't look like the one in the tutorial. After a good amount of time (around 30 minutes) I finally realized what was wrong and switched to the correct part. The part I needed was the XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 5.24.31 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/c5f6334a9cffac4f76c6bd378ab447a84993e220393b033ea58f52fbdca86872.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 5.25.14 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/a9976db49fb4a34c098228fab1678c1e4c2e820f3a07e7e09ad8804278e87d2c.png)

 After that I finished the other parts fairly quickly, I got the buttons environment sensor, oled and MPU6050 in around 1.5 hours. I then proceeded to spend the next hour-ish figuring out how the nets worked. I tried problem solving it myself by eventually decided to use youtube to help me. Once I found a video explaining how it works, the process of making them went by pretty fast.

 After finishing the schematic, I went into making the physical PCB. It took me a while to figure out how all the UI in the PCB editor worked, but after around an hour of troubleshooting, I managed to finish wiring all my parts. It was then that I realized I had an error about a board edge clearance violation. After watching a couple youtube videos I finally managed to figure out how to fix it. I thought that I had finished for the day but when I went back to the starbie tutorial, I realized that I forgot to make the star shape in the edge cuts layer. I then  spent the next hour trying to perfect the shape. It somehow still didn't turn out how I wanted it to but I was to tired to re-do it again (at this point it was around 11:15PM).

Most of the picures are taken on Tuesday october sixth since I forgot to take them yesterday.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 3.30.57 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/8b8f765bab7436883ca360d78dce58e2c993215679655e2c3b2b585dc9b4b989.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 3.31.21 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/7bcc1d8e7acc8af9a948201ddd9ba4026125510caa7e5fdbb1e5b81ad24fa78d.png)

### 2026-10-07 – I realized that my the head of the XIAO wasn't poking out of my edge cuts layer which was a problem since the usb wouldn't be able to get plugged in. I spent around an hour fixing that by making a new

**3h**

I realized that my the head of the XIAO wasn't poking out of my edge cuts layer which was a problem since the usb wouldn't be able to get plugged in. I spent around an hour fixing that by making a new edge cuts outline. I also experimented a little with the image converter tool and added some art to my pcb. Then I spent another hour trying to figure out what error I was getting in the DRC. I knew what the error was already since I had gotten it before, it said that one of my parts was sticking out of the outline but a couldn't see any that were. Then after doing some research I realized that I can click on the error and it would show me where the error is. It turned out that it wasn't sticking out but there wasn't enough of a margin/not enough space between the part and the outline. It took forever to fix but I finally got it!

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 4.48.46 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/7aa66da2e6a00d1c0356a41fbd9f3db2fdb57ae0482f9ade7d33bb0c408a7b9e.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 at 10.59.05 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/150d3444246b115d7317106167df1ddd8dd76d4f269e95b18c3489d8836054ce.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 3.31.21 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/7bcc1d8e7acc8af9a948201ddd9ba4026125510caa7e5fdbb1e5b81ad24fa78d.png)

### 2026-10-07 – Finished re-routing all of my wires (something went wrong)

**3h**

Finished re-routing all of my wires (something went wrong)

I just finished rerouting all of my wires by using different layers so that they don't wrap-around other parts. Discovering more layers lowkey felt magical. But of course, something just had to go wrong. While I was in the long, tiring process of deleting and adding wires, I ended up deleting J1 without noticing. After a while of routing, I felt like it was really empty so I go back to check the github tutorial and what do you know, the biggest piece in the very centre was just missing. I genuinely have no idea how I didn't notice the fact that I deleted the biggest piece there is but somehow it happened, I then had to undo every single change that made for anything after I deleted it and then had to re-wire everything again 😭😔. Although it wasn't the most fun experience, I did learn some things so who knows, maybe it was worth it. Regardless, it's done now and after I add a switch and the batteries, I can finally order my parts.
